newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian crudes firmer, Tapis rises to $1.20 premium.
newsitem.headline: Asian crudes firmer, Tapis rises to $1.20 premium.

text.p: Crude prices in Asia were mostly firmer on Wednesday with news emerging of a Tapis deal at a premium of $1.20.
The 450,000 barrels were sold into South Korea by a producer at the highest premium to date for current November trading.
The last deal was done at a premium of $1.15, although traders said at least one offer into Burma's tender for November Tapis was at $1.40 fob. The tender closed Tuesday.
A further sign of the firmer light sweet market was a deal on Wednesday for 650,000 barrels of Australian Kutubu at Tapis quotes plus 27 cents, pipping the last deal by a cent or two.
The cargo was sold by a European major to Australia, but not into its own system.

Traders said a major is seeking a premium of 65 cents over Arun quotes for a November cargo of North West Shelf. Another seller is looking to be more aggressive after the last deal was done at Arun quotes plus 60 cents.

Paper Tapis firmed in line with recent Brent and NYMEX futures gains. The Tapis paper market, which usually lags futures, rose to $24.55/$24.65 for November quotes compared with a day-earlier level of $24.30/$24.50. Two spreads for first quarter/second quarter were traded at $1.80 between traders.
Elsewhere, Oman was trading at flat to a slight premium in relation to the MPM value. Traders estimated only a handful of cargoes were left to sell in November.

The only other Middle East cargoes left on the shelf for November is a Lower Zakum, held by a major, and Masila crude. A trader said up to 15 November Dubai cargoes have been placed. Traders said 200,000 barrels of November Minas were traded at ICP +20 cents and 100-150,000 barrels of November Widuri at ICP +25 cents.
